Good — the package root already re-exports `export_csv`, so the protected test will import correctly.

Now the only real decision is the **empty-columns edge case**, where the pre-existing `tests/test_export_csv.py` (in scope, written before me) encodes a specific convention: even with zero columns, a header record line is emitted (`"\r\n"`), and each data row emits a record line (`"\r\n"`). Since `csv.writer.writerow([])` already emits exactly `"\r\n"` (an empty record terminated by CRLF), my current implementation **already matches** that convention.

The conflict is only with **my own** newly-added `tests/test_export.py`, which asserts `""`. Since both conventions are defensible from the terse task text, the pre-existing in-repo test is stronger evidence of the intended local contract, and my file is optional/editable. I'll fix **my** test to match the repo's existing convention (keep emitting the header/data record lines for empty columns).
